summary: Iteration 34 — E2E testing of new Leads CRM + Staff role (Phase 1 CRM). Backend 19/19 pytest pass (after fixing a seed-data bug). Frontend 18/19 PASS (1 false-negative). CRITICAL SEED BUG FOUND & FIXED IN-PLACE: the seeded staff account `staff.blr@kmfoundation.online` was created with role='office_admin' in the database (no `staff` role users existed). I corrected the role + permissions directly via Mongo so that the staff scoping rules (assigned-to-me only, no reassign, redirect to /leads, sidebar limited to Overview/Messages/Leads/Settings) could be validated. Main agent must add an idempotent seed for this user.

minor.issue: When staff sends a bogus assignee id, `_validate_assignee` runs and returns 400 BEFORE the staff-role 403 guard fires (the assignee lookup happens to be invoked from a different code path or order). Currently a valid-but-foreign assignee_id from a staff user IS correctly rejected with 403 — verified manually. Low risk; consider checking staff role guard before the assignee lookup for cleaner 403 responses.

The 2 seeded leads (Sneha Prospect, Vivek Enquiry) are not in seed.py either — they may vanish on a fresh DB.
rca of the issue: Seed bug RCA: the staff login account `staff.blr@kmfoundation.online` was created via the API (likely by the main agent through `POST /api/users` while logged in as super_admin) BEFORE confirming role payload, and it ended up with role='office_admin'. There is no `seed_staff` function in /app/backend/seed.py. Mitigation: add `await db.users.update_one({email:'staff.blr@kmfoundation.online'}, {$set:{role:'staff', permissions: STAFF_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS}}, upsert insert if missing)` to seed.py. Reproduction: drop the user → restart backend → log in as staff → observe role='office_admin' from /api/auth/me. Verified fix: after `db.users.update_one` setting role='staff', all 4 previously-failing scoping tests pass.
